subject.paper: Manifold-constrained plasticity enables stable learning in recurrent neural circuits

grade.official_code_inspection_this_run: C blocked by binary redirect/cache transport

right_rotation_invariance.statement: If Eq.34 is Q_next = Q R with R orthogonal k x k, then span(Q_next)=span(Q) and Q_next Q_next^T = Q Q^T exactly. Therefore this operation cannot rotate the imposed k-dimensional structural subspace in ambient R^N.
right_rotation_invariance.implication: Any nonzero principal-angle drift of a k-dimensional empirical subspace under an otherwise exact confinement model must arise from activity leaving the structural span, rank/estimation effects, feedback/covariance dynamics, or code implementing a different transformation; it cannot be caused by the right rotation alone.

nonlinear_confinement_counterexample.setup: N=2, k=1, q=(1,2)/sqrt(5), Q=q, W=Q Q^T, r=2q, I=I_fb=noise=0. Then W r = 2q is in span(Q), but elementwise tanh(2q) is not proportional to q.
nonlinear_confinement_counterexample.implication: For the printed Eq.1, P_perp r_dot = P_perp tanh(Wr)/tau is nonzero in this explicit case, so rank-k recurrent connectivity alone does not guarantee exact state confinement. The paper's exponential-decay argument is insufficient unless the implementation adds projection or operates in a special invariant coordinate structure.

observations: The paper says tanh is applied elementwise and constructs W from a low-rank structural basis.
The paper later describes a continuously evolving manifold basis under rotational drift and reports frozen versus adaptive empirical-subspace alignment differences.

The paper also distinguishes the empirical activity subspace tracked by SPLiT from the imposed structural subspace, so source-level tension is not a paper-wide refutation; the decisive question is what the released code actually projects and rotates.

scope_guard: This does not refute SPLiT, its reported MSE advantages, or the usefulness of adaptive empirical-subspace tracking.
This does not establish that the released code follows the printed equations literally; code inspection remains the decisive next step.
The article was observed as an uncorrected proof, so equation/prose semantics may still receive publisher corrections.
The formal right-rotation result applies only if Eq.34 is implemented as right multiplication by an orthogonal k x k matrix.
The confinement counterexample shows insufficiency of rank-k W plus elementwise tanh, not that the paper's actual simulations materially escaped the intended manifold.
safe_conclusion: The candidate remains scientifically plausible, but the published source cannot yet be used as clean evidence that a structural k-dimensional manifold rotates in ambient space or that low-rank W by itself exactly confines nonlinear state dynamics. The strongest reproducible claim is narrower: SPLiT tracks an empirical activity subspace and the paper reports improved decoding under its tested simulations; interpretation of the rotational-drift mechanism is code-dependent until S1 Code is inspected or independently rerun.
